blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Fundamental Rights are contained in Part III of the Indian Constitution, spanning Articles 12 to 35.
These rights are called 'Fundamental' because they are essential for individual development and enforceable by courts.
Articles 5 to 11 cover Constitutional provisions regarding citizenship at commencement, migration, and parliamentary powers.
Article 11 vests power in Parliament to regulate the right of citizenship.
Questions frequently ask for the Part number of Fundamental Rights: Part III (Articles 12 to 35).
Remember the distinction between Article 6 (Migrants from Pakistan) and Article 7 (Migrants to Pakistan).
Article 11 provides Parliament with the authority to regulate citizenship by law.
